thesis.text: Communication can be treated as a statistical problem whose fundamental limits are set by entropy, channel capacity, and noise.

citations.context: The fundamental problem of communication is that of reproducing at one point either exactly or approximately a message selected at another point.
As was pointed out by Hartley the most natural choice is the logarithmic function.
A physical system, or a mathematical model of a system which produces such a sequence of symbols governed by a set of probabilities, is known as a stochastic process.³
This was constructed with the use of a table of random numbers.⁴
The first-order approximation is obtained by choosing successive letters independently but each letter having the same probability that it has in the natural language.⁵
Stochastic processes of the type described above are known mathematically as discrete Markoff processes and have been extensively studied in the literature.⁶

relations.why: Shannon says he extends their general theory to include noise and statistical structure.

relations.quote: A physical system, or a mathematical model of a system which produces such a sequence of symbols governed by a set of probabilities, is known as a stochastic process.³
relations.why: The reference is given for the mathematical notion of a stochastic process used to model a discrete source.

relations.quote: The first-order approximation is obtained by choosing successive letters independently but each letter having the same probability that it has in the natural language.⁵
relations.why: The reference supplies letter, digram, trigram, and word frequency data for the approximations to English.

relations.quote: These are restatements in terms of the graph of conditions given in Fréchet.

relations.quote: The form of H will be recognized as that of entropy as defined in certain formulations of statistical mechanics⁸ where pi is the probability of a system being in cell i of its phase space.
relations.why: Tolman is cited for the statistical-mechanics definition of entropy that Shannon reuses as information entropy.

relations.quote: This method of encoding is substantially the same as one found independently by R. M. Fano.⁹
relations.why: Fano’s independent method is compared with Shannon’s arithmetic encoding procedure.

relations.quote: This is the famous ergodic theorem or rather one aspect of this theorem which was proved in somewhat different formulations by Birkoff, von Neumann, and Koopman, and subsequently generalized by Wiener, Hopf, Hurewicz and others.³
relations.why: The ergodic theorem is invoked to justify identifying long-sequence averages with ensemble averages.

relations.quote: Wiener has pointed out the intimate relation between the invariance of physical devices under time translations and Fourier theory.⁴
relations.why: Wiener’s work is cited for the statistical and Fourier-theoretic view of communication systems.

relations.quote: If a function of time f (t) is limited to the band from 0 to W cycles per second it is completely determined by giving its ordinates at a series of discrete points spaced 2W seconds apart in the manner indicated by the following result.⁵
relations.why: Shannon cites his own earlier paper for proof and discussion of the sampling theorem used in the continuous theory.
